text:
elaine: heads up — seeing sustained queuing on us-west-2 GPUs for the last 20m. Streaming tails are holding KV caches and preventing non-streaming jobs from making progress. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/queues?region=us-west-2 — 5k queued, ~220 active streams. @tom can you take a look?

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler-bot: scaled up +2 g4dn nodes at 1842506820 due to queue > 2000 (policy=queue_based).

raj: yep — observed the same. Streaming sessions keep long KV caches alive and block batch slot recycling. Currently streaming has no hard cap per-shard. We should consider fair-share or per-customer caps.

sasha: fair-share by weight sounds reasonable, but weight-only can still let many tiny streaming requests dominate total slots. I prefer SLO-driven allocation: allocate guaranteed slots to requests with 95p latency SLO < 200ms, rest go to best-effort.

tom: oncall data — top 3 tenants are 60% of streaming concurrency this morning. If we do per-tenant concurrency limits we can protect smaller customers. Also FYI us-west-2 reserved pools are at ~92% today.

elaine: what about a softer approach: degrade offending streaming sessions to chunked (non-interactive) mode after a grace period, rather than full preemption. That would free KV caches faster but still return partial outputs.

raj: preempting active streams is risky for UX. Fallback to chunked mode is safer. Example config sketch:

```
admission:
  streaming:
    max_concurrent_per_shard: 600
    fallback:
      mode: chunked
      after: 30s
```

sasha: +1 on chunked fallback. We should run evals to pick the right timeout threshold. Also calculate token-cost savings vs user-latency impact before rolling wide.

ling: FYI there's some packet loss to a subset of nodes in us-west-2a — ~1.2% drop for nodes i-abc123/i-def456 which causes reconnect flaps and long-held sockets for streams. Filing a cloud-network ticket. This might be compounding the slot-hold problem.

infra-bot: infra-bot created NET-4281: investigate packet drops for i-abc123,i-def456 in us-west-2a.

tom: proposed action plan for canary today: (1) set streaming soft cap = 60% per-shard (2) enable chunked fallback after 25s for top-traffic tenants (3) enforce per-customer concurrent stream limit = 300 for canary tenants. Roll to us-west-2a, monitor 30m.

elaine: rolling canary now to us-west-2a with config:
```
streaming.soft_cap=0.6
streaming.chunk_timeout=25s
streaming.per_customer_limit=300
```
Watching the queues and KV cache usage charts — will update in 15/30/60.

raj: if canary is good we should add an automatic regression alert: fire when sync queue length > 1000 AND streaming concurrency > 500 for > 10m. Also update docs for fallback behaviour.

sasha: :thumbsup:
